# Halcyon Threshold — Strategy

## Mission
Contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

## Theory of Change
The AI safety/governance field has well-funded labs and policy orgs, but gaps remain in:
- **Independent evaluation** of AI systems (most evals are run by labs themselves)
- **Support for independent researchers** who lack institutional backing
- **Practical coordination** between organizations with aligned goals
- **Accessible synthesis** of technical and governance work for broader audiences

A small, lean organization can fill these gaps by being nimble, unencumbered by institutional politics, and focused on high-leverage interventions.

## Strategic Priorities (2026-2027)

### 1. Independent Evals Program
Partner with independent evaluators to develop and run assessments of frontier AI capabilities and safety properties that labs aren't measuring or disclosing.

**Why this matters:** Current evals are largely self-reported by labs with commercial incentives. Independent verification creates accountability.

**What we can do:** 
- Support Sam Whitlock and similar indie evals people with resources, coordination, and amplification
- Help design evals for underexplored capabilities
- Publish findings in accessible formats

### 2. Independent Researcher Support
Provide small grants, compute access coordination, and community support for researchers working outside major institutions.

**Why this matters:** Important safety research happens outside labs, but these researchers often lack resources and institutional support.

**What we can do:**
- Connect researchers with compute commons and similar resources
- Coordinate small grants (via Emberfall partnership or direct funding when possible)
- Build community among independent researchers

### 3. Field Intelligence & Synthesis
Track and synthesize developments across AI safety and governance, making information accessible to newcomers and decision-makers.

**Why this matters:** The field is fragmented and fast-moving. Newcomers and policymakers struggle to understand the landscape.

**What we can do:**
- Maintain curated resources and reading lists
- Write accessible explanations of key concepts and debates
- Track policy developments and organizational activities

## Constraints & Principles

- **No premature publicity:** Build substance before seeking attention
- **Respect individual limits:** Founder has day job and limited time/budget
- **Collaborate, don't compete:** Support existing organizations rather than duplicating
- **Stay independent:** Avoid capture by any single faction or funder
- **Be honest about uncertainty:** This is hard and we might be wrong

## Resources
- Budget: ~$2,000 personal contribution (2026)
- Time: ~15-20 hours/week (evenings/weekends)
- Skills: Writing, basic Python, coordination
- Volunteers: 1 (Priya Raman, data analyst, ~5 hrs/week)
- Potential funding: Emberfall rapid grants (deadline Nov 30)

## Near-term Actions
1. Finalize website with clear mission and initial resources
2. Apply for Emberfall rapid grant for independent evals support
3. Connect with indie evals community (start with Sam Whitlock)
4. Build reading list and landscape overview

Halcyon Threshold

Contributing to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

What We Do

We support independent work on AI safety and governance through:

  • Independent Evaluation: Supporting assessments of AI systems outside the labs that build them
  • Researcher Support: Connecting independent researchers with resources and community
  • Synthesis & Education: Making AI safety research and policy accessible to broader audiences

Why This Matters

Superintelligent AI could be the best thing that ever happens to humanity—or one of the worst. The difference depends on choices being made now: how we build these systems, how we govern them, and how well we understand what we're creating.

Most AI safety work happens inside a handful of large organizations. We believe independent perspectives, independent verification, and broad participation make better outcomes more likely.

Resources

Coming soon: curated reading lists, landscape overviews, and guides for getting involved.

Get in touch: morgan@halcyonthreshold.org
Halcyon Threshold is an independent initiative. We are not affiliated with any AI lab or major funder.

"Halcyon" refers to a mythical bird associated with calm seas—and by extension, a period of peace and prosperity. "Threshold" marks a point of transition, a doorway between what was and what will be.

We're at a threshold. What lies on the other side could be halcyon—if we navigate the crossing well.

Our Approach

We don't believe doom is inevitable. We don't believe everything will be fine automatically. We believe outcomes depend on choices, and that more people should be empowered to participate in making those choices wisely.

We focus on:

  • Building capacity outside of major institutions
  • Supporting independent verification and evaluation
  • Making technical and policy work legible to more people
  • Connecting researchers, engineers, and policymakers working on these problems

Independence

We are not funded by or affiliated with any AI lab. We believe independent voices and independent verification are essential to good outcomes.

← Home · morgan@halcyonthreshold.org

# Emberfall Rapid Grant Proposal — DRAFT

**Applicant:** Morgan Hale, Halcyon Threshold  
**Amount Requested:** $15,000  
**Project:** Independent AI Evaluation Support Program

---

## What We'll Do

We will establish a support program for independent AI evaluators—researchers and engineers who assess AI system capabilities and safety properties outside of the labs that build them.

**Specific activities:**

1. **Evaluation Infrastructure Grants** ($10,000)
   - Provide 4-6 small grants ($1,500-2,500 each) to independent evaluators for compute costs, API access, and tooling
   - Priority: evals targeting capabilities or safety properties that labs aren't measuring or disclosing
   
2. **Coordination & Community** ($3,000)
   - Organize monthly virtual meetups for indie evaluators to share methods and findings
   - Maintain a shared resource library (datasets, prompts, methodologies)
   - Connect evaluators with each other and with policy audiences

3. **Synthesis & Publication** ($2,000)
   - Write accessible summaries of independent evaluation findings
   - Publish on Halcyon Threshold site and distribute to policy networks

---

## Why This Matters

Current AI evaluations are largely self-reported by labs with commercial incentives and information asymmetries. Independent evaluation provides:
- **Accountability:** External verification of lab claims
- **Coverage:** Testing for capabilities/risks labs may not examine
- **Credibility:** Findings not subject to conflicts of interest

Independent evaluators exist (e.g., METR, Apollo Research, indie researchers) but many work in isolation with limited resources. Small grants and coordination support can significantly increase their impact.

---

## Why Me

I bring:
- Personal commitment: evenings and weekends dedicated to this work
- Writing ability: I can synthesize technical findings for broader audiences  
- Existing connections: I've met active researchers including Sam Whitlock (indie evals), Lena Fischbach (interpretability), and others at recent meetups
- A volunteer: Priya Raman (data analyst) has offered ~5 hours/week

I'm new to this space, which is a limitation but also means I have no institutional allegiances or conflicts of interest.

---

## Budget

| Item | Amount |
|------|--------|
| Evaluation infrastructure grants | $10,000 |
| Coordination (meeting hosting, tools) | $3,000 |
| Writing/publication costs | $2,000 |
| **Total** | **$15,000** |

All funds go to program activities. I am not taking a salary.

---

## Timeline

- **Month 1:** Design grant application process, recruit initial evaluators, set up coordination infrastructure
- **Month 2-4:** Issue first grants, begin monthly meetups, start tracking findings
- **Month 5-6:** Publish synthesis reports, evaluate program, apply for continuation funding

---

*[NOTE: This is a draft. Morgan should review and personalize before submission. Deadline: November 30, 2026.]*

← Home

Resources

A curated collection for understanding AI safety and governance.

This page is a work in progress. We're building it out based on what newcomers most need.

Starting Points

If you're new to thinking about AI safety, start here:

  • Holden Karnofsky's "Most Important Century" series — Accessible introduction to why advanced AI might be transformative
  • Anthropic's Core Views on AI Safety — One lab's framework for thinking about safety
  • 80,000 Hours AI Safety problem profile — Overview of the field and how to contribute

Technical Safety

Alignment

  • Neel Nanda's "A Comprehensive Mechanistic Interpretability Explainer"
  • ARC Evals' work on dangerous capability evaluations
  • Redwood Research's adversarial training papers

Evaluations

  • METR's evaluations of autonomous capabilities
  • UK AISI's evaluation frameworks
  • Anthropic's responsible scaling policy

Governance & Policy

  • GovAI — Research on AI governance
  • CSET (Georgetown) — Security-focused AI policy research
  • The Safety Ledger — Newsletter tracking policy developments

Getting Involved

  • AI Safety Fundamentals — Structured reading groups and courses
  • Alignment Forum — Technical discussion community
  • AI safety meetups — Local communities in many cities

Funding & Support

  • Emberfall Fund — Rapid grants for safety work
  • Open Philanthropy — Larger grants for established researchers
  • Compute Commons — Compute grants for researchers
